name: Cooke Speed Panchro
designer: Horace W. Lee; later Series II associated with Gordon Cook
productionYears: 1930 onward; Series I from 1930, Series II from 1945, Series III wide-angle redesigns circa 1953/1954
cardLabel: Hollywood's defining vintage cinema prime family
publicSummary: The Cooke Speed Panchro is one of the most important cinema lens families ever made. Introduced for cinematographic use around 1930, it brought fast f/2 performance, warm skin tones, gentle contrast, compact optics and the classic early Cooke Look to Hollywood from the sound era through the 1960s, and later returned as a go-to vintage choice for digital period work.
coverage: Originally designed for 35mm motion-picture formats / Super 35-style coverage. Rehoused examples vary. Longer focal lengths can often cover larger sensors, while wider lenses generally remain S35-oriented.
formatCoverageNotes: Original Speed Panchros are best treated as 35mm motion-picture / S35 lenses, not full-frame lenses.
Coverage varies strongly by focal length, series, copy, rehousing and focus distance.
Offshoot Rentals measured a TLS set at approximately: 18mm ≅31mm image circle, 25mm ≅34mm, 32mm ≅32mm, 40mm ≅38mm, 50mm ≅44mm, 75mm ≅45mm.
In that measured TLS set, the 50mm and 75mm could cover ARRI LF Open Gate with caveats, while the wider lenses did not fully cover LF Open Gate.
mounts: Original cine mounts varied by era and camera system
Common vintage mounts include Bell & Howell, Mitchell, Eyemo, Arri Standard and other period mounts depending on lens/copy
Modern rehousings commonly use PL mount

seriesHistory.notes: Cooke traces Speed Panchro origins back to Horace Lee's Cooke Opic lenses, released in 1920, and the Cooke Series O f/2 design era.
Created specifically for cinematographic applications. Cooke states Series I had 13 focal lengths from 24mm to 121mm at f/2.
Coated redesigns with anti-reflective coating, commonly associated with 18mm, 25mm, 32mm, 40mm, 50mm and 75mm focal lengths.
Wide-angle redesigns, especially 18mm and 25mm, associated with larger angular fields for widescreen-era requirements.

focalLengths: Series I: 24mm to 121mm range according to Cooke; commonly cited 1935 cinema set includes 24, 28, 32, 35, 40, 50, 75 and 108mm
Series III: redesigned wide angles, especially 18mm and 25mm
Common modern rehoused sets: 18, 25, 32, 40, 50, 75 and 100mm; some sets add 35mm, 152mm or related Deep Field/Telepanchro companions
tStops: Series I: f/2 across the 24mm to 121mm range according to Cooke's own historical article
Coated / later sets: commonly around T2.2-T2.3 for 18mm through 75mm, with 100mm commonly around T2.8
Modern rehoused measurements vary by rehousing company and individual lens
closeFocus: Original close focus varies by lens, original mount and rehousing; use copy-specific data when available.
Modern TLS-style rehoused examples often achieve very close focus: approx. 8 inches on 18mm/25mm, 9 inches on 32mm, 13 inches on 40mm, 15 inches on 50mm, 2 feet 4 inches on 75mm and 2 feet on 100mm.

focalLengthSpecs.coverage: S35-oriented; approx. 31mm image circle in one measured TLS set
focalLengthSpecs.notes: Often listed as Series III in modern rehoused sets; original examples and rehousing specs vary.

focalLengthSpecs.series: Series II / Series III depending on copy
focalLengthSpecs.coverage: S35; approx. 34mm image circle in one measured TLS set
focalLengthSpecs.notes: Common key focal length; Series III version was a wide-angle redesign.

focalLengthSpecs.coverage: S35; approx. 32mm image circle in one measured TLS set
focalLengthSpecs.notes: Common modern rehoused set focal length.

focalLengthSpecs.series: Series I / II depending on copy
focalLengthSpecs.closeFocus: 11 in in one TLS spec table
focalLengthSpecs.notes: Important early Speed Panchro focal length; not always included in modern 6/7-lens sets.

focalLengthSpecs.coverage: S35; approx. 38mm image circle in one measured TLS set
focalLengthSpecs.notes: Often a hero focal length for the Panchro look; Tom Sigel relied mostly on the 40mm for the first act of Bohemian Rhapsody.

focalLengthSpecs.coverage: S35; approx. 44mm image circle in one measured TLS set; may cover LF Open Gate with some vignetting depending on copy/focus
focalLengthSpecs.notes: One of the most iconic Speed Panchro focal lengths.

focalLengthSpecs.coverage: S35; approx. 45mm image circle in one measured TLS set; can cover LF Open Gate in that measured set

focalLengthSpecs.series: Deep Field Panchro / companion focal length
focalLengthSpecs.coverage: Varies; often paired with Speed Panchro sets
focalLengthSpecs.notes: Often listed as Cooke Deep Field Panchro 100mm rather than a standard Speed Panchro.

focalLengthSpecs.maxAperture: T3.2 in some rehoused rental sets
focalLengthSpecs.closeFocus: 4 ft 9 in in some rehoused rental sets
focalLengthSpecs.coverage: Likely larger than the wide lenses, but copy-specific
focalLengthSpecs.notes: Not part of every Speed Panchro set; include as a related/companion focal length when present.

opticalFormula: Family of fast spherical cinema prime designs descended from Cooke Opic / Series O f/2 thinking. Exact optical formulas vary by focal length and series. Treat the Speed Panchro as a lens family rather than one fixed formula.
coating: Series I examples are often uncoated or early single-coated depending on copy/era; Series II introduced anti-reflective coating; coatings and condition vary heavily by individual lens.
designFamily: Cooke Opic / Series O / Speed Panchro spherical cinema primes
rehousingInfo: Many surviving Speed Panchros have been rehoused by companies such as TLS, P+S Technik, Van Diemen and others. Rehousing typically adds PL mount, modern focus and iris gears, common fronts, improved close focus and more robust mechanics while retaining vintage optical blocks.
lookSummary: Warm, gentle, face-friendly vintage spherical rendering with soft contrast, smooth focus roll-off, compact optical blocks, painterly separation, creamy bokeh and beautiful but sometimes aggressive flare. Wide open, they can feel soft/smeary in the best way; stopped down they become cleaner while retaining warmth.
characteristics: Creamy bokeh with possible swirl or cat's-eye shapes depending on focal length and stop
Can flare strongly, especially uncoated or worn examples
Small optical blocks and compact original mechanics
Strong copy-to-copy variation because of age, coating, rehousing and service history
S35-first coverage, with longer focal lengths sometimes covering larger sensors
strengths: One of the defining cinema lens families of the sound-era Hollywood look
Fast f/2-era performance made them extremely important when sound production limited noisy arc lighting
Very flattering on faces and skin
Strong historical connection to classic Hollywood
Highly useful today for period films, digital softening, nostalgic looks and painterly contrast
Modern rehousings make vintage optics practical on contemporary PL-mount cameras
weaknesses: Not full-frame as a family; coverage varies and wider lenses are S35-oriented
Original mechanics are often not practical without rehousing
Can flare heavily and lose contrast
Wide-open performance can be soft or smeary compared with modern lenses
Exact specs differ across Series I, II, III, Deep Field Panchro and rehoused variants

famousUses.title: Wings
famousUses.role: historical Cooke usage / early Academy Award-era citation
famousUses.notes: Cooke states Speed Panchros became Hollywood's lens of choice from the 1920s through the 1960s, citing Wings as the first Academy Award winner in that lineage.

famousUses.notes: ShotOnWhat lists Mitchell BNC camera and Cooke Speed Panchro lenses; IMDb also lists Cooke Speed Panchro and Astro-Berlin Pan Tachar lenses.

famousUses.title: Casablanca
famousUses.role: classic Hollywood Cooke Speed Panchro citation
famousUses.notes: Cooke's own history page cites Casablanca as part of the Speed Panchro era.

famousUses.title: The Sound of Music

famousUses.notes: Cooke's own history page cites The Sound of Music as part of the Speed Panchro era.

famousUses.title: Bohemian Rhapsody
famousUses.role: vintage Speed Panchros used for the first act

curationNotes: This entry is designed as a complete LensWiki family/milestone entry. Use focalLengthSpecs for the tool UI table. Exact values should be marked copy-specific where the data comes from modern rehoused examples rather than original factory datasheets.
notes: Speed Panchro history is messy because Series I, II, III, Deep Field Panchro companions and modern rehousings are often discussed together. The safest public presentation is to treat this as a family entry, then optionally create separate sub-entries later for Series I, Series II, Series III, Deep Field Panchro 100mm and modern Panchro/i Classic/SP3 descendants.
